item.title: White House confirms Quad leaders' meeting in Manila on sidelines of ASEAN Summit
item.description: The White House itinerary confirms that US President Donald Trump will participate in a multilateral meeting with Quad leaders in Manila on Tuesday, November 17, marking the first in-person Quad ...
item.content:encoded:
White House confirms Quad leaders' meeting in Manila on sidelines of ASEAN Summit  The White House itinerary confirms that US President Donald Trump will participate in a multilateral meeting with Quad leaders in Manila on Tuesday, November 17, marking the first in-person Quad leaders' summit in two years on the sidelines of the ASEAN Summit. ANI | Updated: 16-11-2026 12:52 IST | Created: 16-11-2026 12:52 IST

A visitor walks past the White House and a new flag pole installed on the North Lawn in Washington, DC, US. (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The White House itinerary confirmed that US President Donald Trump will participate in a multilateral meeting with Quad leaders in Manila on Tuesday, November 17, marking the first in-person Quad leaders' summit in two years, on the sidelines of the ASEAN Summit. Following his arrival at Manila's Ninoy Aquino International Airport, US President Donald Trump is scheduled to welcome the Quad leaders for an official photo opportunity, which will be immediately followed by the high-level multilateral meeting. The strategic alignment comes as the regional grouping recalibrates its footprint. The Quad was formed in 2007 but became largely inactive the following year amid concerns about provoking China. Donald Trump revived the grouping in 2017 to address growing concerns over China's increasing economic, diplomatic and military influence in the Indo-Pacific, although he did not hold a leaders' summit during his earlier term. The Manila meeting will be the first Quad leaders' meeting during his current term as US President, following five ministerial-level sessions since Trump began his second term on January 20, 2025. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio had indicated last month that the Quad leaders could meet on the sidelines of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit in Manila, where the Philippines is hosting the gathering as the current chair of the 11-member ASEAN. Against this diplomatic backdrop, India has joined the United States and several partner nations in executing a new pact designed to protect critical technologies and artificial intelligence (AI) supply chains amid growing concerns about Beijing's acquisition of advanced technology, particularly high-end semiconductor processors. This diplomatic step comes as Washington intensifies oversight of the movement of advanced Nvidia microchips into China, following a recent controversy involving the company's Chief Executive, Jensen Huang, and his association with an individual flagged by American authorities over suspected ties to Chinese intelligence. The agreement is designed to reduce reliance on supply networks controlled by Beijing and strengthen cooperation among allied states across vital technological domains. Specifically, New Delhi has joined the San Francisco Declaration on the Secure Foundations of Enduring Prosperity, alongside the US, Japan, Australia, Israel, the United Kingdom, South Korea, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates. The accord functions as a core component of Washington's broader Pax Silica initiative, which seeks to build robust and dependable supply networks for the global artificial intelligence sector, encompassing semiconductors, critical minerals, advanced manufacturing, energy infrastructure and data hubs. The San Francisco Declaration aims to establish a unified framework among participating nations to identify and protect technologies and infrastructure considered vital to the development of artificial intelligence. The initiative recognises that the global AI supply chain spans multiple jurisdictions. While a semiconductor might originate on a drawing board in one country, the fabrication equipment could come from another, with transportation and final deployment involving several additional territories. US Under-Secretary of State for Economic Affairs Jacob Helberg told the Financial Times that this distribution makes international collaboration essential for safeguarding the technological ecosystem. "The know-how to design a chip, the machine that makes it and the port that ships it can all be in different countries," Helberg said. He further noted that the pact makes the security of critical technologies and supporting infrastructure a collective responsibility shared among Pax Silica partners. Signatory states are expected to establish dedicated working groups to identify vulnerabilities, share intelligence and explore the creation of economic hubs capable of attracting investment in AI-linked industries. Launched in December 2025, Pax Silica represents a Washington-led framework aimed at strengthening cooperation across the entire AI and semiconductor spectrum. Its scope extends beyond chip manufacturing to include essential minerals, energy inputs, advanced production methods, AI infrastructure and logistics networks, seeking to reduce overreliance on centralised supply chains and prevent states from using control over critical resources as instruments of economic coercion. India formally joined the Pax Silica coalition in February 2026 during the India AI Impact Summit, making the recent San Francisco Declaration another step towards expanding multilateral partnerships. The agreement comes as Washington expresses serious concerns about Beijing's acquisition of advanced American AI processors, particularly those manufactured by Nvidia. The US has consistently restricted direct shipments of advanced semiconductor hardware to China over concerns that such capabilities could strengthen Beijing's military apparatus and artificial intelligence capabilities. Nevertheless, chip shipments through third-party countries and the use of offshore data facilities have emerged as significant challenges for American export regulations. US President Donald Trump has reportedly ordered a strict crackdown on companies suspected of illegally diverting advanced Nvidia microchips to China, bringing renewed attention to indirect channels through which advanced American technology could reach Chinese entities despite direct trade restrictions. Earlier this month, foreign ministers representing the Quad alliance, comprising India, the US, Japan and Australia, announced plans to provide more than USD 85 million in technical and financial assistance to expand access to trusted AI infrastructure across the Indo-Pacific. This was alongside a separate USD 10 million allocation from Washington to support critical mineral recycling efforts across India and ASEAN member states. The new agreement comes as Trump prepares to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping this week at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, amid intense strategic competition between Washington and Beijing over leadership in advanced technologies. (ANI)

item.title: Trump administration to name Nvidia, Microsoft among over two dozen AI “national champions”: Report
item.description: The Trump administration plans to designate over two dozen US companies, including Nvidia, Amazon, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Anthropic, as AI "national champions." The initiative aims to help American ...
item.content:encoded:
Trump administration to name Nvidia, Microsoft among over two dozen AI “national champions”: Report  The Trump administration plans to designate over two dozen US companies, including Nvidia, Amazon, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Anthropic, as AI "national champions." The initiative aims to help American tech firms compete globally against Chinese rivals by offering expedited export licenses and federal support. ANI | Updated: 16-11-2026 12:04 IST | Created: 16-11-2026 12:04 IST

US President Donald Trump (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The Trump administration is reportedly preparing to designate Nvidia, Amazon, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic, along with more than two dozen other American companies, as artificial intelligence "national champions", a strategic initiative aimed at helping US technology firms expand into overseas markets and compete with Chinese rivals. According to sources cited by The Wall Street Journal, the formal announcement is expected within the coming week, with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick set to lead the announcement, although the timeline remains subject to change. The programme aims to encourage foreign governments and commercial entities to adopt US-developed artificial intelligence systems rather than Chinese alternatives. The framework brings together American processors, AI architectures and related products into streamlined packages to simplify procurement for foreign buyers. Companies selected for this status may receive expedited authorisations for export licences, official support for international operations and eligibility for federal funding mechanisms, as detailed on the Commerce Department's initiative portal. Initially unveiled approximately a year ago as a key component of the Trump administration's broader technology strategy, the specific list of designated companies had remained undisclosed until now. The initiative underscores Washington's determination to expand the global reach of American AI innovation amid growing strategic competition with Beijing. Chinese competitors, including Huawei Technologies, have aggressively expanded into overseas markets across Europe and Latin America to strengthen their position in the global technology landscape. Nvidia's anticipated selection comes amid increased regulatory scrutiny of the company and evolving US frameworks governing exports of advanced artificial intelligence chips to China. Nvidia's hardware powers many of the world's most sophisticated AI systems, making its products highly sought after. President Donald Trump has frequently praised the company and its Chief Executive, Jensen Huang, for building a domestic technology giant that plays a crucial role in the AI revolution. However, concerns over national security and potential vulnerabilities that could allow Chinese entities to obtain high-end Nvidia components through export-control loopholes have prompted calls for stricter restrictions. The Wall Street Journal noted that disclosures concerning Huang's alleged links to a Chinese intelligence operative have intensified pressure from critics urging that national security take precedence over commercial dominance. Lutnick has also faced criticism over allegations that the Commerce Department failed to close loopholes that could potentially allow Chinese companies to access advanced Nvidia microchips. The publication previously indicated his reluctance to alienate Beijing during trade negotiations. The upcoming announcement coincides with Lutnick's preparations to accompany Trump on a scheduled diplomatic visit to China this week. Meanwhile, the Commerce Department is expected to advance new regulations aimed at preventing the illicit diversion of high-performance processors to Beijing. Expanding US artificial intelligence exports has remained a cornerstone of the Trump administration's agenda since last summer, with the initiative framed as a vital mechanism for maintaining American leadership in a critical sector where Washington and Beijing are competing for global supremacy. (ANI)

item.title: "Will be able to deter aggression": Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit says keeping close watch on China
item.description: Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit on Monday said that India is keeping a close eye on China and has the "plans in place" for deterrence.
item.content:encoded:
"Will be able to deter aggression": Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit says keeping close watch on China Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit on Monday said that India is keeping a close eye on China and has the "plans in place" for deterrence.  ANI | Updated: 16-11-2026 11:57 IST | Created: 16-11-2026 11:57 IST

Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit (Photo/ANI). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

India

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit on Monday said that India is keeping a close eye on China and has the "plans in place" for deterrence. Addressing a session titled 'Preparing India's Armed Forces & Future Wars' at the ANI National Security Summit 3.0 in New Delhi, Air Chief Marshal Dixit said that the Indian armed forces have inducted new technology. When asked about China, he said, "We are keeping a very close eye, and we monitor each and every activity that is happening in our adversaries. That is our adversaries; that is our peacetime job, and align our procedures first and then capability along with it. So the aircraft or the capability, actually, their use depends on three-four things. So whether their crew is trained, whether they are in network-centric warfare, and the altitude at which they are, will be able to affect us." "Considering all these things, our plans are in place. So we add some new technology we are inducting. So, along with that, it is okay; we are in an okay situation and not a simple but okay situation that we will be able to deter this aggression... We are in a situation which is called no peace, no war and from there we may shift over to some kind of offensive or defensive," Air Chief Marshal Dixit added. India has maintained that peace and tranquillity in the border areas were essential to normalising India-China relations. Last month, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar stressed that any disturbance along the border would have consequences. Speaking in a conversation with John Micklethwait, Editor-in-Chief of the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in Delhi, Jaishankar said India and China have no agreed border and that the issue has persisted for decades. "We don't have an agreed border between India and China. This is not a new issue; it's been going on for multiple decades... From 1975 till 2020, a good 45 years, no blood was shed on that border. The last time there were fatalities was in 1975. In this period, India-China relations did grow," he said. (ANI)

item.description: "Gadi Eisenkot’s unhinged incitement against Prime Minister Netanyahu and his office is appalling. While the prime minister extends a hand of unity, Eisenkot and his colleagues issue inflammatory, ...
item.content:encoded:
"Unhinged incitement": Likud accuses Gadi Eisenkot of inflammatory remarks against Netanyahu, questions allegations against Israeli PM’s chief of staff "Gadi Eisenkot’s unhinged incitement against Prime Minister Netanyahu and his office is appalling. While the prime minister extends a hand of unity, Eisenkot and his colleagues issue inflammatory, incendiary statements every day in venomous language," the party said. ANI | Updated: 16-11-2026 11:57 IST | Created: 16-11-2026 11:57 IST

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Israel's ruling Likud Party has accused opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot of making inflammatory remarks against caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his office, describing his statements as "unhinged incitement" while questioning allegations surrounding the Israeli Prime Minister's Chief of Staff. In a post on X, Likud slammed Eisenkot, accusing him of issuing provocative statements even as Netanyahu had extended an invitation to form a national unity government. "Gadi Eisenkot’s unhinged incitement against Prime Minister Netanyahu and his office is appalling. While the prime minister extends a hand of unity, Eisenkot and his colleagues issue inflammatory, incendiary statements every day in venomous language," the party said. Defending Netanyahu's Chief of Staff, Likud said the official had acted in accordance with his obligations by passing information to the police regarding suspected serious criminal activity. "Eisenkot is inciting against the chief of staff, a law-abiding citizen who passed information to the police about suspected serious criminal activity, as he was obligated to do," the party said. Questioning the allegations against the official, Likud added, "Did the chief of staff plant the envelopes of cash with the suspects? The absurdity of Eisenkot’s unhinged incitement is outrageous." The latest exchange comes amid an escalating political confrontation between Netanyahu and Eisenkot over the formation of Israel's next government and allegations surrounding the Prime Minister's Office. Netanyahu had earlier urged Eisenkot to enter negotiations without preconditions to establish a national unity government, arguing that Israel required a broad political coalition to address its security challenges, particularly the threat posed by Iran. In a video statement, Netanyahu said his recent conversation with Eisenkot had reinforced his belief in the need for a broad-based government, adding that a narrow coalition or one dependent on parties he described as supporters of terrorism would be unable to address the country's security challenges. He also called for political differences to be set aside and proposed that the issue of military conscription could be resolved through discussions involving representatives of the Haredi community. However, Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, dismissed Netanyahu's overture as "another spin", saying that negotiating teams from Likud and Yesh Atid had already scheduled a meeting. Eisenkot further maintained that any national emergency government formed under his leadership would require acceptance of his proposed principles and a break with extremist political forces. The political standoff follows last month's election, after which Netanyahu's bloc lost its parliamentary majority. Eisenkot received the mandate to form a government from Israeli President Isaac Herzog last week. Meanwhile, Finance Minister and Religious Zionism Party chairman Bezalel Smotrich backed Netanyahu's appeal for unity, urging Eisenkot to accept the proposal and describing it as an opportunity for national responsibility. (ANI)
